title: Check yourself: stateful stages and side effects

questions.stem: Per this page, how many elements does `sorted()` process in `stream.sorted().limit(5)`?

options.text: Only the first five, since `limit(5)` cuts the stream before sorting
options.says: The page says that happens for limit(5).sorted(); in sorted().limit(5) the sort comes first.

options.text: Only the five smallest, since it keeps a small heap as it goes
options.says: The page describes sorted() as stateful: it must see all elements before producing output.

options.text: Every element of the stream, since it has to see them all first
options.says: The page says sorted().limit(5) sorts all elements, while limit(5).sorted() sorts only the first five.

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens when a pipeline that saves each element to a database from `peek()` ends in `findFirst()`?

options.text: Some elements are never saved, because the run stops at the first match
options.says: The page warns that peek may not execute once a short-circuit fires early, and says to use forEach() or collect first instead.

options.text: All of them are saved, since `peek()` sits ahead of the `filter()` step
options.says: The page's own example puts peek ahead of filter and still says it will NOT save if the short-circuit fires early.

options.text: Each one is saved as it passes, since `peek()` ignores how the run ends
options.says: The page says the opposite: a short-circuiting terminal operation can stop peek from running, so some elements are never saved.
